Q: Splitting website css and js files into smaller riles or combining them in 2025 A:

As many files as you want in development but use a webpacker in production. You do not want the client making a bazillion requests (unless you do, because you're evil and want to flood the dev tools network tab as a form of obfuscation). Because keep in mind every request contains headers and latency. The fewer requests the better - keep it safe and simple and less things break. A lot of websites don't do this, and it boggles my mind. Numerous asynchronous requests is why you get so many FOUCs these days (flashes of unstyled content). Go to youtube on a public library computer and you will see what I mean.

Minifcation helps but at this point it doesn't matter as much considering servers may choose to serve their content using gzip, which is done at a layer that the front end dev has no access to and need not worry about. In other words minifying or not, the actual data over the wire will be about the same due to how compression works - what matters is the entropy of the data, not how much there is. Minifying code or serving "huge javascript files" only matters when the web host has strict storage requirements.

Regardless there is now a front-end api for this - CompressionStream and DecompressionStream iirc, these can compress/decompress gzip streams on the fly, so if you want to manually do this you can probably write a simple bundler on the backend and parser on the frontend for yourself. https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/CompressionStream

Q: can you help Create a memory management program using either the fifo page replacement approach or the lru approach A:

It supports both FIFO and LRU and prints a table plus total page faults.

Logic

  • FIFO: Replace the page that has been in RAM the longest (front of the list); new page is appended.

  • LRU: Keep (page, last_use_index); on replacement, remove the one with smallest index (least recently used), then add the new page and update its index on each reference.

def fifo(pages, frames):
    ram = []
    faults = 0
    result = []
    for p in pages:
        fault = p not in ram
        if fault:
            faults += 1
            if len(ram) < frames:
                ram.append(p)
            else:
                ram.pop(0)
                ram.append(p)
        row = [str(p)] + [str(x) for x in ram] + [""] * (frames - len(ram))
        row.append("F" if fault else "")
        result.append(row)
    return result, faults


def lru(pages, frames):
    ram = []  # list of (page, last_use_index)
    faults = 0
    result = []
    for i, p in enumerate(pages):
        fault = True
        for j, (pg, _) in enumerate(ram):
            if pg == p:
                ram[j] = (p, i)
                fault = False
                break
        if fault:
            faults += 1
            if len(ram) < frames:
                ram.append((p, i))
            else:
                ram.sort(key=lambda x: x[1])
                ram.pop(0)
                ram.append((p, i))
        row = [str(p)] + [str(x[0]) for x in ram] + [""] * (frames - len(ram))
        row.append("F" if fault else "")
        result.append(row)
    return result, faults


def main():
    algo = input("Algorithm (FIFO / LRU): ").strip().upper()
    while algo not in ("FIFO", "LRU"):
        algo = input("Enter FIFO or LRU: ").strip().upper()
    pages = list(
        map(
            int,
            input(
                "Page sequence (e.g. 7 0 1 2 0 3 0 4 2 3 0 3 2 1 2 0 1 7 0 1): "
            ).split(),
        )
    )
    frames = int(input("Number of page frames: "))

    if algo == "FIFO":
        table, faults = fifo(pages, frames)
    else:
        table, faults = lru(pages, frames)

    header = ["Page"] + [f"Frame {i+1}" for i in range(frames)] + ["Fault"]
    width = max(len(str(x)) for row in table for x in row)
    width = max(width, max(len(h) for h in header))
    sep = "+" + "+".join("-" * (width + 2) for _ in header) + "+"
    print(sep)
    print("|" + "|".join(f" {h:^{width}} " for h in header) + "|")
    print(sep)
    for row in table:
        print("|" + "|".join(f" {str(c):^{width}} " for c in row) + "|")
    print(sep)
    print(f"\nTotal page faults: {faults}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Q: Postgres "Error: SASL: SCRAM-SERVER-FIRST-MESSAGE: client password must be a string" A:

I had the same problem, apparently the config didn't recognize the before password so I had to create a new one on the terminal

sudo -u postgres psql 

ALTER USER username WITH PASSWORD 'your new password with quotes around';

not only that, because I was using pgAdmin, for it to connect I had to close and then open so I can input the new password. After that everything just started working.
